observations: Teal and black cordless drill housed in a blue plastic carrying case.
Two slide-on batteries are present, one attached to the drill and one loose.
A battery charger with a European/Nigerian style two-pin plug is included.
The case contains various accessories: 6 drill bits, 6 screwdriver bits, 9 sockets, and an orange flexible bit extension.
The drill has a manufacturer's label on the side, but the text is illegible due to low image resolution.
A watermark 'MCKENNY TOOLS' is visible across the center of the image.

claims.evidence: The battery labels are not visible in the photo to confirm the voltage.
The mode selector ring behind the chuck is not clear enough to see an impact/hammer icon.
The tool is a compact, handheld cordless model.
Photo 0 shows the tool with detachable batteries and no power cord.

risks.proof: A video showing the drill driving a screw into a piece of wood to demonstrate torque and battery stamina.
risks.if_unproven: as having dead or non-functional batteries

risks.proof: A clear, high-resolution photo of the manufacturer's rating plate on the side of the drill.
A photo of the label on the bottom or side of the batteries.
risks.if_unproven: as a 12V or 18V system (36V is often a marketing exaggeration for this size)

risks.proof: A video of the drill running, showing the chuck spinning and the speed trigger working.

proof_requests: Clear, close-up photo of the label/rating plate on the side of the drill.
Photo of the specifications label on the batteries.
Video of the drill operating, including switching between gears and modes.
Close-up photo of the torque and mode selector ring.
response.reason: The brand and technical specifications (voltage and impact function) are unreadable in the provided photo. Because the price difference between a genuine professional brand and a generic clone is significant, verification is required.
